then.text: Coal for Trevithick's engine, is it? You've had your bucket already, bach. Don't waste it. It's the good stuff.

else.text: Merthyr, is it? An engine to fire for the wager? Hah. Take this, then.
Best Rhondda steam coal. Dry, hard, burns hot and nearly smokeless, which is why the Navy bought it by the shipload.
Bore da! I was fifteen when I first went underground. We called it 'going down the hole', as if it was a hobby.
Rhondda steam coal was the best in the world. Low in smoke, hot as a dragon's breath. The Royal Navy ran on it.
Lewis Merthyr, this was. The shafts are still down there. Mind the display cases; they're older than I am.

rhn_heritage_visitor.text: I came for the winding gear and I stayed for the tea. The man at the till says the lamp was only ever a flame behind a wire gauze. The Davy lamp, they call it.
Sir Humphry Davy designed it in 1815 so a flame couldn't ignite the gas, and the colour of the flame told a miner whether the air was bad.
